metadata.title: Noise-Contrastive Estimation: A New Estimation Principle for Unnormalized Statistical Models
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Estimation of unnormalized statistical models
nodes.statement: Given i.i.d. samples of $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ from an unknown pdf $p_d(\cdot)$, estimate $\alpha$ such that $p_d(\cdot) = p_m(\cdot;\alpha^\star)$ where $p_m(\cdot;\alpha) = p_m^0(\cdot;\alpha)/Z(\alpha)$ and $Z(\alpha)$ is intractable.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimate parameters of a parametric statistical model whose density is known only up to an intractable normalization constant.

nodes.name: Unnormalized model with explicit normalization parameter
nodes.statement: For an unnormalized pdf $p_m^0(\cdot;\alpha)$, include the (log-)normalization constant as an additional parameter: $\ln p_m(\cdot;\theta) = \ln p_m^0(\cdot;\alpha) + c$ with $\theta = \{\alpha, c\}$, where $c$ estimates $-\ln Z(\alpha)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Augment the model parameters with a scalar c that estimates the negative log-partition function, treating normalization as just another parameter.

nodes.name: Noise-contrastive objective $J_T(\theta)$
nodes.statement: Given data $X = (x_1,\ldots,x_T)$ and noise $Y = (y_1,\ldots,y_T)$ with $y_t \sim p_n(\cdot)$, define $J_T(\theta) = \frac{1}{2T} \sum_t \ln h(x_t;\theta) + \ln[1 - h(y_t;\theta)]$, where $h(u;\theta) = r(G(u;\theta))$, $G(u;\theta) = \ln p_m(u;\theta) - \ln p_n(u)$, and $r$ is the logistic function.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical objective contrasting log-density of data versus noise through the logistic function.

nodes.name: Noise-contrastive estimator $\hat{\theta}_T$
nodes.statement: $\hat{\theta}_T = \arg\max_{\theta} J_T(\theta)$, the maximizer of the noise-contrastive objective.
nodes.statement_clean: The NCE estimator is the parameter value that maximizes the empirical contrastive objective.

nodes.name: Population objective $J(\theta)$ and functional $\tilde{J}(f)$
nodes.statement: $J(\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2} \, \mathbb{E}\big[\ln h(x;\theta) + \ln(1 - h(y;\theta))\big]$, and $\tilde{J}(f) = \tfrac{1}{2} \, \mathbb{E}\big[\ln r(f(x) - \ln p_n(x)) + \ln(1 - r(f(y) - \ln p_n(y)))\big]$ viewed as a function of $f(\cdot) = \ln p_m(\cdot;\theta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Population (infinite-sample) version of the NCE objective and its rewriting as a functional of the log-density.

nodes.name: Noise-weighted matrix $I$ and weight $P(x)$
nodes.statement: $I = \int g(x) g(x)^T P(x) p_d(x) dx$ where $P(x) = p_n(x) / (p_d(x) + p_n(x))$ and $g(x) = \nabla_\theta \ln p_m(x;\theta)|_{\theta^\star}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Information-like matrix that controls NCE consistency and asymptotic variance; reduces to a weighted Fisher information when P(x) is constant.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Nonparametric estimation)
nodes.statement: $\tilde{J}$ attains a maximum at $f(\cdot) = \ln p_d(\cdot)$, and there are no other extrema if the noise density $p_n(\cdot)$ is nonzero whenever $p_d(\cdot)$ is nonzero.
nodes.statement_clean: In the nonparametric (infinite-data) limit, the unique maximizer of the NCE objective is the true log-density of the data.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Consistency)
nodes.statement: If conditions (a)–(c) hold, then $\hat{\theta}_T \xrightarrow{P} \theta^\star$: (a) $p_n$ is nonzero whenever $p_d$ is; (b) $\sup_\theta |J_T(\theta) - J(\theta)| \xrightarrow{P} 0$; (c) $I$ has full rank.
nodes.statement_clean: Under positivity of the noise, uniform convergence of the empirical objective, and full-rank of I, the NCE estimator is consistent.
assumptions: (c) $I = \int g(x) g(x)^T P(x) p_d(x) dx$ has full rank

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Asymptotic normality)
nodes.statement: $\sqrt{T}(\hat{\theta}_T - \theta^\star)$ is asymptotically normal with mean zero and covariance $\Sigma = I^{-1} - 2 I^{-1} \big(\int g(x) P(x) p_d(x) dx\big)\big(\int g(x)^T P(x) p_d(x) dx\big) I^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The NCE estimator has a Gaussian limit distribution with an explicit asymptotic covariance.

nodes.name: Corollary 1 (MSE rate)
nodes.statement: For large $T$, the mean squared error $\mathbb{E}\,\|\hat{\theta}_T - \theta^\star\|^2$ behaves like $\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma)/T$.
nodes.statement_clean: The asymptotic MSE of NCE decays as the trace of the asymptotic covariance divided by sample size.

nodes.name: Connection to logistic regression
nodes.statement: $J_T(\theta)$ equals (up to factor $1/2T$) the log-likelihood of logistic regression discriminating data $X$ from noise $Y$ with class-conditional densities $p(\cdot|C{=}1) = p_m(\cdot;\theta)$ and $p(\cdot|C{=}0) = p_n(\cdot)$ and equal class priors.
nodes.statement_clean: NCE is logistic-regression discrimination of data versus noise; this links unsupervised density estimation to supervised classification.

nodes.name: Noise-equal-to-data gives twice the Cramér–Rao bound
nodes.statement: If $p_n = p_d$, the asymptotic covariance $\Sigma$ in Theorem 3 equals twice the Cramér–Rao bound; hence noise close to the data distribution yields MSE close to the statistical optimum.
nodes.statement_clean: Choosing the noise distribution close to the data distribution provides a near-optimal MSE guarantee for NCE.

nodes.name: Desiderata for the noise distribution $p_n$
nodes.statement: $p_n$ should (1) be easy to sample from, (2) admit an analytical log-pdf, and (3) yield small $\mathbb{E}\|\hat{\theta}_T - \theta^\star\|^2$. Practical choices include Gaussian, uniform, Gaussian mixtures, or ICA distributions.
nodes.statement_clean: Practical guidelines for selecting the contrastive noise distribution.

nodes.name: Logistic discriminator $h(u;\theta)$
nodes.statement: $h(u;\theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp[-G(u;\theta)]}$ with $G(u;\theta) = \ln p_m(u;\theta) - \ln p_n(u)$.

nodes.name: Posterior class probability under equal priors
nodes.statement: $P(C=1|u;\theta) = \frac{p_m(u;\theta)}{p_m(u;\theta) + p_n(u)} = h(u;\theta)$, $P(C=0|u;\theta) = 1 - h(u;\theta)$.

nodes.name: Noise-Contrastive Estimation (NCE)
nodes.statement: Maximize $J_T(\theta)$ over $\theta = \{\alpha, c\}$ to obtain $\hat{\theta}_T$, by treating estimation as logistic discrimination of data vs noise.
input: Unnormalized model $p_m^0(\cdot;\alpha)$ and noise log-pdf $\ln p_n(\cdot)$

nodes.name: Sample contrastive noise and form discriminator
nodes.statement: Draw $T$ noise samples $y_t \sim p_n(\cdot)$, set $\ln p_m(u;\theta) = \ln p_m^0(u;\alpha) + c$, and define $G(u;\theta) = \ln p_m(u;\theta) - \ln p_n(u)$, $h(u;\theta) = r(G(u;\theta))$.

nodes.name: Maximize $J_T(\theta)$ via conjugate gradient
nodes.statement: Iteratively update $\theta = \{\alpha, c\}$ to increase $J_T(\theta) = \frac{1}{2T} \sum_t \ln h(x_t;\theta) + \ln(1 - h(y_t;\theta))$ using a gradient-based optimizer (e.g. conjugate gradient).

nodes.name: Return $\hat{\theta}_T$
nodes.statement: Return the maximizer $\hat{\theta}_T = (\hat{\alpha}, \hat{c})$; the estimate of $-\ln Z(\hat{\alpha})$ is $\hat{c}$.

nodes.name: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
nodes.statement: Maximize $J_{MLE}(\alpha) = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t \ln p_m^0(x_t;\alpha) - \ln Z(\alpha)$, requiring an analytical (or closed-form) expression for the partition function $Z(\alpha)$.

nodes.name: MLE with importance sampling
nodes.statement: Approximate $Z(\alpha) \approx \frac{1}{T} \sum_t p_m^0(n_t;\alpha)/p_{IS}(n_t)$ with $n_t \sim p_{IS}(\cdot)$ and use the resulting gradient estimate inside MLE.

nodes.name: Contrastive Divergence (CD)
nodes.statement: Approximate the gradient $\nabla_\alpha Z(\alpha)/Z(\alpha) = \int p_m(n;\alpha) \nabla_\alpha p_m^0(n;\alpha) dn$ by drawing $n_t$ via short MCMC (e.g. one step of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with three leapfrog steps) initialized at the data.

nodes.name: Score Matching (SM)
nodes.statement: Minimize $J_{sm}(\alpha) = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t,n} \tfrac{1}{2} \Psi_n^2(x_t;\alpha) + \Psi_n'(x_t;\alpha)$ with $\Psi_n(x;\alpha) = \partial_{x_n} \ln p_m^0(x;\alpha)$.

nodes.name: ICA model with Laplacian sources
nodes.statement: Data $x = As \in \mathbb{R}^4$ where $A$ is a $4\times 4$ mixing matrix and the components of $s$ are i.i.d. unit-variance Laplacian. Unnormalized model: $\ln p_m^0(x;\alpha) = -\sum_{i=1}^4 \sqrt{2}\,|b_i x|$ with $\alpha$ the rows $b_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: A 4-dimensional ICA model with Laplacian sources used to benchmark NCE against MLE, importance sampling, contrastive divergence, and score matching.

nodes.name: Two-layer patch model of natural images
nodes.statement: Patch model $\log p_m(x;\theta) = \sum_n f_{th}\big( \ln[v_n (Wx)^2 + 1] + b_n \big) + c$ trained by NCE with uniform-on-sphere noise on whitened $30\times 30$ image patches; recovers Gabor-like first-layer (“simple cells”) and pooling second-layer (“complex cells”).
nodes.statement_clean: Energy-based two-layer model of whitened natural-image patches, trained with NCE, yielding simple- and complex-cell-like features.

nodes.name: Markov random field for natural images
nodes.statement: MRF $\log p_m(I;\theta) = \sum_{\xi,i} f_{th}\big(\sum_{\xi'} w_i(\xi') I_w(\xi+\xi') + b_i\big) + c$ with $7\times 7$ filters and clique size 15 pixels, trained on whitened $45\times 45$ patches by NCE; learns high-frequency Gabor-like filters.
nodes.statement_clean: Markov random field model of natural images trained by NCE; recovers Gabor-like filters without norm constraints.
